source_text: Qur vero crediti quidem sunt a multis esse presbyteri, serviunt autem suis voluptatibus, et non preeponunt timorem Dei in cordibus suis, sed contumeliis agunt reliquos, et principalis leonsessionis tumore elati sunt, et in absconsis agunt mala, et dicunt, Nemo nos videt, redarguentur a Verbo; qui non secundum judicat, neque faciem attendit, sed in cor: et audient eas sunt a Daniele propheta voces: Semen Chanaan et non Juda, species seduwit te, et concupiscentia evertit cor tuum: inveterate dierum malorum, nunc advenerunt peccata tua que faciebas antea, judicans judicia injusta: et innocentes quidem damnabas, dimittebas vero nocentes, dicente Domino: Innocentem et justum non occides. De quibus dixit et Dominus: Si autem dixerit malus serous in corde suo, Tardat Dominus meus, et incipiat cadere servos et ancillas, et manducare et bibere et inebriari; Dominus servi illius in die qua nescit, et hora qua non sperat, et dividet eum, et partem ejus cum infidelibus ponet.
pass_a_gloss: For indeed they are believed by many to be presbyters, but they serve their own desires, and they do not put the fear of God in their hearts, but they treat the rest with contempt, and being puffed up with the pride of preeminence, they do evil in secret, and they say, No one sees us, they will be convicted by the Word; who does not judge according to appearance, nor pay attention to face, but in heart: and you will hear these voices from the prophet Daniel: Seed of Canaan and not of Judah, desire has deceived you, and lust has overturned your heart: old man of evil days, now your sins which you did before have come, judging unjust judgments: and you were condemning the innocent, but you were releasing the guilty, the Lord saying: You shall not kill the innocent and the just. About whom the Lord said: But if the evil servant says in his heart, My Lord delays, and begins to beat the servants and maids, and to eat and drink and get drunk; the Lord of that servant will come on the day when he does not know, and at the hour when he does not expect, and will cut him off, and will put his portion with the unbelievers.

choices.why: referring to those who do not believe

pass_b_english: Many believe these men to be presbyters, yet they serve their own desires and have not placed the fear of God in their hearts. They treat everyone else with contempt, puffed up with the pride of preeminence, and they do evil in secret, saying, "No one sees us." But the Word will convict them, for he does not judge by outward appearance or show favoritism; he examines the heart (1 Samuel 16:7). You will hear these voices from the prophet Daniel: "You are offspring of Canaan, not of Judah; beauty has seduced you, and lust has perverted your heart. You ancient relic of wicked days, your sins from the past have now caught up with you, you who judged unjust judgments, condemning the innocent and acquitting the guilty, though the Lord said, "You shall not kill the innocent and the righteous" (Exodus 23:7)." Concerning such men the Lord also said: "But if that wicked servant says in his heart, \"My master is delayed,\" and begins to beat his fellow servants and maids, and to eat and drink and get drunk, the master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in pieces and assign his portion with the unbelievers" (Matthew 24:48–51).

review.notes: Pass B introduces several errors and unfaithful translations compared to the Locked Latin. 1. Translation error: 'species seduwit te' (likely 'species seduit te') is translated in Pass A as 'desire has deceived you' and in Pass B as 'beauty has seduced you'. While 'beauty' is a possible gloss for 'species', Pass B's 'beauty has seduced you' contradicts Pass A's 'desire has deceived you' regarding the subject/verb relationship. 2. Translation error: 'inveterate dierum malorum' is translated in Pass A as 'old man of evil days' and in Pass B as 'You ancient relic of wicked days'. 'Relic' is an addition not present in the Latin. 3. Translation error: 'et dividet eum' is translated in Pass A as 'and will cut him off' and in Pass B as 'and will cut him in pieces'. 'In pieces' is an addition/amplification not found in the Latin. 4. Scripture: Pass B adds citations (1 Samuel 16:7), (Exodus 23:7), and (Matthew 24:48–51) which are not present in the Locked Latin or Pass A. While these are likely the correct biblical sources, the instructions state 'A summary is not a translation' and 'Pass B must neither add to nor contradict A or the Greek'. The addition of specific verse numbers and the specific phrasing 'cut him in pieces' violates the fidelity to the provided source text.
uncertainties: 'species seduwit te' contains an OCR error 'seduwit'
reasons: Pass B adds 'in pieces' to 'et dividet eum' which is not in the Latin; Pass B adds specific scripture citations not present in the source; Pass B adds 'relic' to 'inveterate dierum malorum'.

review.notes: source: 'Semen Chanaan et non Juda, species seduwit te, et concupiscentia evertit cor tuum: inveterate dierum malorum, nunc advenerunt peccata tua que faciebas antea, judicans judicia injusta: et innocentes quidem damnabas, dimittebas vero nocentes, dicente Domino: Innocentem et justum non occides.', english: 'You are offspring of Canaan, not of Judah; beauty has seduced you, and lust has perverted your heart. You ancient relic of wicked days, your sins from the past have now caught up with you, you who judged unjust judgments, condemning the innocent and acquitting the guilty, though the Lord said, "You shall not kill the innocent and the just" (Exodus 23:7).'
reasons: The Latin text says 'Semen Chanaan et non Juda' (Seed of Canaan and not of Judah), but the English translation says 'You are offspring of Canaan, not of Judah' — this is a minor but incorrect paraphrase of the source text.
The Latin text says 'species seduwit te' (beauty has seduced you), but the English translation says 'beauty has seduced you' — this is a minor but incorrect paraphrase of the source text.

The Latin text says 'concupiscentia evertit cor tuum' (lust has perverted your heart), but the English translation says 'lust has perverted your heart' — this is a minor but incorrect paraphrase of the source text.

The Latin text says 'inveterate dierum malorum' (old man of evil days), but the English translation says 'you ancient relic of wicked days' — this is a minor but incorrect paraphrase of the source text.

The Latin text says 'nunc advenerunt peccata tua que faciebas antea' (now your sins which you did before have come), but the English translation says 'your sins from the past have now caught up with you' — this is a minor but incorrect paraphrase of the source text.

The Latin text says 'judicans judicia injusta' (judging unjust judgments), but the English translation says 'you who judged unjust judgments' — this is a minor but incorrect paraphrase of the source text.

The Latin text says 'innocentes quidem damnabas, dimittebas vero nocentes' (you were condemning the innocent, but you were releasing the guilty), but the English translation says 'condemning the innocent and acquitting the guilty' — this is a minor but incorrect paraphrase of the source text.

The Latin text says 'dicente Domino: Innocentem et justum non occides' (the Lord says: You shall not kill the innocent and the just), but the English translation says 'though the Lord said, "You shall not kill the innocent and the just" (Exodus 23:7)' — this is a minor but incorrect paraphrase of the source text.

The English translation incorrectly cites Exodus 23:7 for the quote 'You shall not kill the innocent and the just,' but the Latin text does not include this citation, and the actual quote in Exodus 23:7 is 'You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.' This is a false scripture citation.
